Common startup helper for radr functions

Source: R/radr.R
radr_startup.Rd

Perform standard radr initialisation steps inside a function:

  • print a header with tgbase::function_header();

  • record execution date/time;

  • record and temporarily modify global options (e.g. width, future.globals.maxSize);

  • start a timing object with tgbase::tic().

The function returns a small list with everything needed for a matching teardown helper. You should typically pair this with radr_teardown() inside an on.exit() call in the calling function.

Usage

radr_startup(f.name, verbose = TRUE, width = 70L)

Arguments

f.name

(character) Name of the calling function (e.g. "read_vcf"). Used only for logging in tgbase::function_header().

verbose

(logical) When TRUE, the helper prints the execution date/time and passes verbosity to the teardown helper. Default: verbose = TRUE.

width

(integer) Temporary value for getOption("width"). Default: width = 70.

Value

A named list containing:

  • file.date – character timestamp "YYYYMMDD@HHMM";

  • old.dir – working directory to restore;

  • opt.width – original options("width");

  • opt.future – original options("future.globals.maxSize");

  • timing – timer object from tgbase::tic();

  • f.name – function name;

  • verbose – verbosity flag.
